mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with positive 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with an increase in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of decreasing PAYEMS and increasing UNRATE does not correlate with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with positive 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decrease does not correlate with negative 60-day returns during tightening cycles (p > 0.05).
